title: Identity proofs
instruction: Check the identity at true size on four pieces we publish, and see the stacked lockup that replaced L2.
intro: These proofs set the wordmark, ampersand B and the lockmark at true size on four pieces we publish: the site’s masthead, a social avatar, a link-preview card and a letterhead. Each follows the rules in chapters 03, 04 and 08, and the fifth proof is the record of the stacked lockup that replaced L2.

groups.label: Masthead on the site
text: L3 in the 1440 px site bar and L1 in the 390 px phone bar, on one left edge (Rule 03.6).

items.label: Site and phone
items.caption: Use Fit to window to see the site bar whole on a smaller screen.

groups.label: Avatar
text: Ampersand B alone on the Charcoal tile, as Rule 04.7 sets it for social avatars and the app icon. The platform prints our name beside the avatar, so the mark can be B alone.

items.label: Upload, feed and app icon
items.caption: At 32 px in a feed, B still reads, where any lettered mark would set its capitals under the 14 px floor.

groups.label: Social card
text: The 1200 by 630 link-preview card, with its specifications under it. Its sign-off passes Rule 08.2’s feed test at 500 and 360 px wide.

items.label: Link-preview card
items.caption: Until chapter 23 sets social cards, build one from these specifications.

groups.label: Letterhead
text: US Letter, 8.5 by 11 inches, at true size on screen, 96 px to the inch. Check the print proof’s scale with a ruler before you judge it on paper.

items.label: US Letter
items.caption: The address, recipient and letter are invented, and the letter is signed with Dustin’s name and title.

groups.label: L2 beside S1
text: On November 7, 2026, Dustin Cathcart, our founder and editor, approved S1, the stacked lockup that sets OATH & over ACTION, in place of L2. Each pair sets L2 at left and S1 at right at the same cap height, at three sizes, so anyone can check the change at true size.

items.label: Three sizes
items.caption: S1 reads in the name’s order with B at the size of the capitals, and it runs about a fifth narrower than L2 at every size.
